data.narrative:
Enigma is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Jonathan Jacobi and Gal Niv, both former Unit 8200 operatives with prior roles at Microsoft and Check Point. The company has raised $71M to date. The relevant peer universe consists of 9 private robotics companies (including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI) and 1 public comparable.

Given Enigma's early stage and the fragmentation of peer data, a stage-progression methodology proves most applicable. Using the $71M in total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a standard 2.5x multiplier for progression from Seed to the next institutional funding round yields an implied valuation of $178M. A peer-median approach was not viable; while 10 same-sector companies exist, fewer than three comparable data points emerged within sufficiently narrow filters (same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier), making cross-sectional comparison unreliable and introducing unacceptable bias.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $151M to $204M, centered at $178M. This range carries material uncertainty given reliance on a single methodological anchor and limited public market reference points in the sector. Key sensitivities include the appropriateness of the 2.5x step-up assumption for this specific founder profile and market window, and whether private market comps—once sufficient data accumulates—would support or contradict this range.
